newsitem.title: CHINA: China sheep wool price to fall in late 1996.
newsitem.headline: China sheep wool price to fall in late 1996.

text.p: China's sheep wool prices are expected to fall in the second half of the year due to heavy imports and may not rise in the next two years, the Market Daily said on Monday.
Huge imports of sheep wool had weakened domestic demand for wool and resulted in big stockpiles in major production areas, the newspaper said.

Although the buying price of sheep wool in northwestern Xinjiang province had dropped to 10,000-10,500 yuan per tonne in 1996 from 13,000-14,000 yuan per tonne in 1995, there were few buyers, it said.
The newspaper forcast that wool prices on the domestic market were unlikely to rebound in the next two years.
China's demand for sheep wool is about 300,000 tonnes per year while its annual output of top quality pure sheep wool is 100,000 tonnes, it said.
As a major wool importer, China imported 283,700 tonnes of wool in 1995 and more than 310,000 tonnes in 1994, it said. It imported 128,255 tonnes in the first seven months, Customs figures showed.

Total domestic output of sheep wool in 1996 was forecast at more than 270,000 tonnes, of which 60,000 tonnes would come from Inner Mongolia, 1,000 tonnes more than in the same period last year, an earlier report said.
